question: Two students discuss a hollow conducting sphere that carries a net charge $+Q$. There is no charge placed inside the cavity. What is the electric field at the center of the sphere? Explain the reason for your answer.

options.A: Zero — In electrostatic equilibrium all excess charge resides on the outer surface, so any Gaussian surface inside the cavity encloses zero charge; the field inside is zero.
options.B: Nonzero and proportional to Q/R² — Field lines must radiate from the center by symmetry.
options.C: Depends on shell thickness — Thicker shells reduce the field at the center.
options.D: Infinite — Curvature near the inner surface concentrates the field at the center.
